name: worst-case-tls
summary: A three-certificate SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f chain with localhost SANs: the largest chain a TLS server would realistically present.
description: The fixture to point a TLS server at. Three SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f certificates - root, intermediate, leaf - put roughly 150 KB of Certificate message on the wire, against a TLS record limit of 16 KB and handshake buffers that were sized when chains were 4 KB. The leaf carries serverAuth and localhost SANs over both IPv4 and IPv6, so it drops straight into a local server without a hostname-mismatch error masking the size failure you are actually testing for.
breaks: TLS handshake buffers sized for pre-quantum chains (the Certificate message spans many records)
Clients and middleboxes that cap the total certificate chain size
Handshake timeouts on constrained or high-latency links, from the extra round trips
Path builders that re-parse the whole chain per candidate path
